result.markdown: --- title: "[Graph.simple_cycles()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method}" body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 toc-depth: 3 page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Find all simple cycles in the graph. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L9336-L9430){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python Graph.simple_cycles(length_bound=None) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} A simple cycle is a closed path where no node appears more than once (except that the first and last node are the same). This method works for both directed and undirected graphs. For directed graphs, uses Johnson's algorithm which is efficient and finds each cycle exactly once. For undirected graphs, uses a backtracking DFS approach that finds all elementary cycles by starting from each node and exploring all paths that return to the starting node. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [length_bound]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [int | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Optional maximum cycle length. If specified, only cycles with at most this many nodes are returned. If `None` (default), all cycles are returned regardless of length. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [list[list[int]]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : A list of cycles, where each cycle is a list of node IDs forming the cycle. The start node is not repeated at the end. ::: ## Technical Notes {.doc-technical-notes} - for directed graphs: `O(V + E)(C + 1)` where `C` is the number of cycles - for undirected graphs: Can be exponential in worst case - unlike `get_cycles()`, this method works for both directed and undirected graphs - cycles are represented as sequences of node IDs without repeating the start node - for undirected graphs, each cycle is returned only once (canonicalized) ## Examples {.doc-examples} Unlike `get_cycles()`, this also works on undirected graphs. A directed graph with a 2-cycle and a 3-cycle produces exactly two simple cycles: ::: {#2012c914 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ( ec.Graph(directed=True) .add_node(label="A") .add_node(label="B") .add_node(label="C") .add_edge(source="A", target="B") .add_edge(source="B", target="C") .add_edge(source="C", target="A") # closes A -> B -> C -> A .add_edge(source="B", target="A") # closes A -> B -> A ) len(graph.simple_cycles()) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` 2 ``` ::: ::: An undirected triangle has exactly one cycle, since each direction around the loop is the same cycle: ::: {#bc9c36f9 .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} graph = ( ec.Graph(directed=False) .add_node(label="A") .add_node(label="B") .add_node(label="C") .add_edge("A", "B") .add_edge("B", "C") .add_edge("C", "A") ) len(graph.simple_cycles()) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` 1 ``` ::: ::: `length_bound=` excludes any cycle longer than the given size -- here, the 4-cycle is filtered out, leaving only the 2-cycle: ::: {#3ee6d7ef .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} graph = ( ec.Graph(directed=True) .add_node(label="A") .add_node(label="B") .add_node(label="C") .add_node(label="D") .add_edge(source="A", target="B") .add_edge(source="B", target="A") # 2-cycle .add_edge(source="B", target="C") .add_edge(source="C", target="D") .add_edge(source="D", target="A") # 4-cycle ) graph.simple_cycles(length_bound=3) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=3} ``` [[1, 2]] ``` ::: :::
